title: kate-core: score a letter after any numeric scalar
summary: digit_hump adds 8 after any numeric scalar, including a fullwidth digit. An ASCII digit still adds 8. The test goes in the existing fuzzy tests module.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: fuzzy.rs has one test module named tests. Add the new test function at the end of that module, before its closing brace. Do not write a second mod tests. Change only the condition in digit_hump. Keep the let-else. let Some(previous) = index.checked_sub(1).and_then(|at| chars.get(at).copied()) else { return 0; }; The condition is one if. if previous.is_numeric() && chars[index].is_ascii_alphabetic() { 8 } else { 0 }. Do not nest an if inside an if. Do not write if numeric { if letter }. Do not touch fuzzy_match, score_one, boundary_bonus, gap_adjust, camel_bonus, next_index, or same_fold. The existing tests a_digit_hump_adds_eight and a_lower_letter_after_a_digit_adds_eight stay at score 47 with positions 0 and 2. Do not rewrite those assertions. The test a_fullwidth_digit_hump_adds_eight calls fuzzy_match of ab and a, U+FF12, B. The hit is Some with score 55 and positions 0 and 2. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep the change under about 60 lines. Run the full test module named in the commands, not only the new test.

regression_tests.name: fuzzy::tests::a_fullwidth_digit_hump_adds_eight
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main. ab against a, U+FF12, B scores 47. After the change the score is 55 and the positions are 0 and 2. ab against a2B stays 47.
